title: Choose Touchline's new visual world
question: The roll assigned The Matchday Programme. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Matchday Programme
options.lineage: 80s and 90s club matchday programmes: duotone cover photos, team sheets, sponsor strips, programme numbers
options.thesis: Every screen is printed like the programme you buy at the turnstile: players appear as two-colour halftone portraits in their club's colours, and line-ups read like the team sheet.
options.viewport: Material shell. Home opens on the week's big match as a programme cover: both clubs' best players as halftone portraits in their club colours, the fixture in condensed type, win/draw/loss as a printed three-part strip. Below: 'Ready for the Big Five' prospects, 'Can't-live-without' team sheet, manager effect table.
options.risk: Halftone must stay legible at small sizes; needs a real shader (Flutter fragment shader) with a plain duotone fallback.

raised.raise: Fixtures and odds update like a scoreboard: values change in place, rows never jump.
A visible column grid: every number sits on the same baseline grid as the programme's stats pages.
One item owns the top of each screen (the cover), everything else is the inside pages.

options.label: The Football Yearbook
options.lineage: Rothmans / Sky Sports Football Yearbook: the stats bible
options.thesis: The app as the yearbook every stats fan owned: dense tables, tiny precise type, a club-colour thumb index down the edge.
options.viewport: Home as the yearbook's 'season at a glance' page: compact tables of prospects, managers and dependencies, club thumb-tabs on the right edge.
options.risk: The most familiar choice here and closest to the editorial-almanac look many AI designs land on; can feel dry for a casual fan.

options.label: Scoreboard Flaps
options.lineage: split-flap boards and old stadium scoreboards
options.thesis: Fixtures, odds and rankings as a black flap board where values clack into place.
options.viewport: Home as a board of this week's fixtures with win chances flapping in.
options.case: Strong for fixtures and odds (clear, glanceable) but thin for player stories, career curves and scouting.
options.risk: Dark board everywhere; reads as a gimmick beyond the fixture list.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.case: Loses both: no football resonance, and grid letters slow reading.
options.kept: A visible column grid for numbers.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Loses both: one item per screen hides the comparisons stats need.
options.kept: One item owns the top of each screen.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.case: Loses both: generic tech look, no football world.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.case: Loses both: charming but unrelated to football.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.case: Already offered last round and passed over.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: FotMob / OneFootball done impeccably: dark cards, crests, stat rows, a single accent.
canonCard.viewport: Fixture list, stat cards, league tabs.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps fans already use, by design.
